note: Ten example queries the QA sweep runs against a deployment. Each one names what a healthy run must produce, so a pass is a claim about behaviour rather than 'it returned 200'. Chosen to span the axes that matter: viewpoint, activity domain, length, licence, source pinning, and two that should legitimately come back thin.

queries.query: first-person cooking footage with hands visible, long continuous takes
egocentric electronics assembly or soldering, head-mounted camera
first-person bike or car repair, hands working on the machine
first-person doing laundry and folding clothes, hands visible
exocentric fixed-camera footage of someone assembling furniture
public egocentric video datasets for hand-object interaction research
first-person warehouse picking and packing footage
first-person footage of glassblowing with both hands in frame
queries.note: Deliberately narrow. Nothing is asserted about the count — the point is that every kept clip still clears the 600s floor and every exclusion still carries a reason, which the universal invariants check.

pipeline_note: Task queries for the whole-pipeline run (qa/run_pipeline.py): search, collect, index, clean, annotate, curate, then audit the clips that came out. These are phrased as tasks rather than as footage descriptions, because that is how a training-data request actually arrives — 'someone doing the laundry', not 'egocentric footage with hands in frame'. Each one costs real money to run: a download through Apify, a minute of Datalake indexing and a caption pass per clip.

pipeline_queries.query: someone doing the laundry, loading a machine and folding clothes
kitchen tasks — chopping, stirring, washing up
fixing a bike, hands on the chain and brakes
packing a suitcase, folding and placing clothes into luggage
assembling flat-pack furniture with a screwdriver and an allen key
